title: Uniqueness of the Planet Earth

competencies.text: Explain Earth's characteristics supporting life versus other planets.

days.title: Conditions for Life
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will explain the characteristics of Earth that support life and compare Earth with other planets.

🌍 The Only Known Home of Life

Of the eight planets in our Solar System, only Earth is known to support life. Scientists point to a combination of conditions working together:

ConditionWhy it mattersOn Earth
Liquid waterSolvent for life's chemical reactionsAbout 71% of the surface is covered by water
Suitable temperatureKeeps water liquid; enzymes workAverage about 15 °C
AtmosphereProvides O₂ and CO₂; traps heat; ozone blocks UV78% N₂, 21% O₂, plus trace gases
Right distance from the SunNot too hot, not too cold (habitable zone)About 150 million km (1 AU)
Magnetic fieldDeflects charged particles from the solar windMade by the moving molten iron outer core
Energy sourcePowers photosynthesis and food chainsSunlight

🔗 They Work Together

No single condition is enough. Distance from the Sun gives the right energy; the atmosphere holds the heat and keeps water from boiling off; the magnetic field helps protect the atmosphere. Remove one, and the others may fail.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Why is LIQUID water considered essential for life?

choices.label: It dissolves substances for life's reactions
It is the only substance that can store sunlight
It makes the planet heavier so gravity is stronger
It blocks all ultraviolet light from the Sun

scenario.explanation: Water is an excellent solvent; cells need it to dissolve and transport substances for their chemical reactions.

choices.label: Movement of molten iron in the outer core
Sunlight bouncing off the ocean surface
Magnetic rocks found in the mountains
The Moon's gravity pulling on the deep oceans

scenario.explanation: Flowing liquid iron in the outer core generates electric currents that create the magnetic field.

scenario.text: What is the main job of the ozone layer?

choices.label: Absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation
Producing the oxygen we need to breathe
Holding liquid water on the planet's surface
Creating the magnetic field around the Earth

scenario.explanation: Ozone (O₃) in the stratosphere absorbs much of the Sun's harmful UV radiation.

days.title: Earth vs Its Neighbors
days.content:
🪐 Comparing the Inner Planets

PlanetAverage surface temperatureAtmosphereWhy no known life
MercuryAbout −180 °C at night to 430 °C by dayAlmost noneNo air to hold heat or water; extreme swings
VenusAbout 464 °CVery thick, about 96% CO₂Runaway greenhouse effect; no liquid water
EarthAbout 15 °CN₂ and O₂, moderate thickness—
MarsAbout −63 °CVery thin, mostly CO₂Too cold and thin for liquid water at the surface; weak magnetic field

🔍 What We Learn

  • Venus is called Earth's "sister planet" because of its similar size, yet it is the hottest planet — its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat. Distance alone does not decide temperature.
  • Mars shows evidence of ancient rivers and has ice at its poles. Scientists search there for signs of past microbial life, following the water.
  • Earth's moderate atmosphere is "just right" — the Goldilocks idea.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term or planet to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Solvent needed by all known life
match.why: It dissolves and transports substances in cells.
It is found in the stratosphere.

match.right: Deflects charged particles of the solar wind
Distance where liquid water can exist
match.why: Not too hot, not too cold.
A runaway greenhouse effect traps heat.
Too cold for liquid water at the surface today.

match.right: Almost no atmosphere; huge temperature swings
match.why: Without air, heat escapes at night.

match.right: Main energy source for life on Earth
match.why: It powers photosynthesis and food chains.

days.title: Special Properties of Water and Air
days.content:
💧 Water's Life-Saving Properties

  • High heat capacity: water heats and cools slowly, so oceans keep coastal climates mild and our body temperature steady.
  • Ice floats: solid water is less dense than liquid water. Lakes freeze from the top down, and the ice layer insulates the water below, so aquatic life survives winter.
  • Universal solvent: dissolves nutrients and carries them in blood and sap.
  • Exists in three states at Earth's temperatures, driving the water cycle that brings rain inland.

🌬️ The Atmosphere as a Blanket and Shield

  • Greenhouse gases keep Earth about 33 °C warmer than it would be without them (you will study this next week).
  • Most small meteors burn up before reaching the ground.
  • It spreads heat around the globe through winds, reducing extreme differences between day and night.

🧭 Comparing Evidence

When scientists judge if a planet could support life, they look for evidence of liquid water, a stable temperature, an energy source and the right chemistry — not just one factor.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Reason about Earth's uniqueness. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: Scientists searching for life on Mars focus on finding signs of water. Why?

choices.label: All known life depends on liquid water
Water is the easiest thing to photograph
Mars is completely covered by oceans today
Water produces oxygen as soon as it freezes

scenario.explanation: Every living thing we know needs liquid water. Where water existed, life might have existed too.

scenario.text: Venus is about the same size as Earth but has a surface temperature of about 464 °C. What is the MAIN reason?

choices.label: Its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps enormous heat
It is the planet closest to the Sun of all
It has no atmosphere, so sunlight hits directly
Its magnetic field produces extra surface heat

scenario.explanation: Venus has a runaway greenhouse effect. It is even hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the Sun.

scenario.text: If Earth lost its magnetic field, what would MOST likely happen over a long time?

choices.label: The solar wind would slowly strip the air away
The oceans would immediately freeze solid overnight
Earth would stop rotating on its axis
Sunlight would no longer reach Earth

scenario.explanation: The magnetic field deflects charged particles. Without it, the solar wind could gradually erode the atmosphere, as is thought to have happened on Mars.

scenario.text: Why do coastal towns like those in Ilocos have milder temperatures than inland areas far from the sea?

choices.label: Water heats and cools slowly, moderating the air
Sea breezes carry cold snow down from the mountains
The sea reflects all sunlight back into space
Coastal towns are located farther from the Sun

scenario.explanation: Water's high heat capacity means the sea warms slowly by day and cools slowly by night, keeping nearby air temperatures more even.

scenario.text: Why is it important for life that ice floats instead of sinking?

choices.label: Ice on top insulates the water below it
Floating ice adds extra oxygen to the water beneath it
Ice that sinks would make the ocean too salty
Floating ice produces heat that warms all fish

scenario.explanation: If ice sank, lakes and seas could freeze from the bottom up. Floating ice keeps the water underneath liquid for aquatic life.

days.title: Why Earth Must Be Protected
days.content:
⚖️ A Delicate Balance

Earth's life-supporting conditions are not guaranteed forever. Human activities can change them:

  • Greenhouse gas emissions thicken the heat-trapping blanket, warming the planet — a small step in the direction of Venus.
  • CFCs once thinned the ozone layer. The Montreal Protocol (1987), which the Philippines joined, phased them out, and the ozone layer is slowly recovering — proof that global action works.
  • Water pollution reduces the clean freshwater that life depends on; only about 3% of Earth's water is fresh, and most of it is frozen.

🌏 The Search for Other Worlds

Astronomers have found thousands of planets around other stars. A few lie in their star's habitable zone, but none has yet been confirmed to host life. Until then, Earth is the only planet we know that can support us.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: Which planet is called Earth's sister because of its similar size?

choices.label: Venus
Mars
Mercury
Jupiter

escape.explanation: Venus is close to Earth in size and mass, but its atmosphere makes it extremely hot.

escape.text: About what percentage of Earth's surface is covered by water?
escape.explanation: About 71% of Earth's surface is water; about 97% of all Earth's water is salty ocean water.

escape.text: Which planet has the HIGHEST average surface temperature?

choices.label: Venus
Mercury
Mars
Earth

escape.explanation: Venus (about 464 °C) is hotter than Mercury because its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat.

escape.text: Why is Earth's distance from the Sun described as the Goldilocks zone?

choices.label: It lets water stay liquid on the surface
It is the closest distance to the Sun
It is where planets have no atmosphere at all
It makes the year exactly 365 days

escape.explanation: At Earth's distance, temperatures allow liquid water — not too hot (boiling away) and not too cold (all frozen).

escape.text: What did the Montreal Protocol help protect?

choices.label: The ozone layer
The magnetic field
The deep ocean
The Moon's orbit

escape.explanation: The agreement phased out ozone-depleting chemicals like CFCs, and the ozone layer is recovering.

escape.text: Which statement BEST explains why Earth supports life?

choices.label: Several conditions work together in balance
Only its distance from the Sun matters
Only its large amount of ocean water matters
Only its strong gravity holds life down

escape.explanation: Water, temperature, atmosphere, magnetic field and energy all interact; no single factor is enough.
